headline: Brigham nurses postpone planned strike as members prepare to vote on contract offer
dek: The Massachusetts Nurses Association withdrew its Oct. 14 walkout notice after Mass General Brigham made a final proposal, but no contract has been ratified and the vote date is not set.
body: More than 4,000 nurses at Brigham and Women’s Hospital in Boston will not begin the open-ended strike they had scheduled for Oct. 14, at least for now. The Massachusetts Nurses Association has withdrawn the strike notice so members can review and vote on a final contract proposal from Mass General Brigham. [WCVB reported](https://www.wcvb.com/article/brigham-nurses-union-postpones-strike-ahead-of-contract-vote/74101163) that the postponement came after the latest bargaining session, while [Mass General Brigham’s statement](https://news.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/bwh-potential-nursing-strike-oct-10) described the offer as its last, best and final proposal.

The change removes the immediate Oct. 14 deadline, but it does not settle the dispute. No ratification vote date has been announced, and the offer is not a contract until nurses approve it. If members reject the proposal, the union could resume strike planning; the hospital’s statement says the MNA agreed to bring the offer to its members rather than proceed with the indefinite walkout. The practical result for patients is a pause in the escalation, not a guarantee that the labor conflict is over.

Mass General Brigham said the two sides reached the point after 13 hours of negotiations in their 27th bargaining session. Under the hospital’s description, the proposed agreement would run from ratification through Sept. 30, 2028. It would add a 2.5% top step to each pay scale upon ratification and another 2.5% top step effective Sept. 30, 2027. The proposal also includes a 2.5% employee contribution for individual post-tax health coverage only for nurses hired into 40-hour positions after ratification; the hospital says current regularly scheduled 40-hour nurses would not see an increased premium share while they remain in that position.

Those terms are the hospital’s account of its proposal, not a jointly announced tentative agreement. The nurses’ union told WCVB that it had made compromises during bargaining but objected to the absence of cost-of-living wage increases. The MNA characterized the hospital’s position as harmful to nurses and patient care. Those are labor-side claims, and they remain contested; the available statements do not establish that the offer will pass or that either side has abandoned its broader arguments about staffing and compensation.

The dispute has already disrupted the hospital once this year. Nurses held a one-day strike on July 8, followed by a four-day lockout, according to earlier union and hospital accounts. The MNA later authorized an open-ended strike by a 93% vote and gave notice of the Oct. 14 action. The union has sought stronger permanent staffing, limits on temporary or traveling nurses, health-insurance choices and compensation it says keeps pace with the cost of living. Mass General Brigham has said it is prepared to maintain patient care during a strike with experienced replacement nurses and contingency plans.

Brigham and Women’s is one of Boston’s major hospitals, so the bargaining outcome reaches beyond the employees at the negotiating table. A prolonged walkout could affect staffing, scheduling and the use of temporary clinicians across a hospital that provides complex specialty care. The postponement gives patients and hospital leaders more time to plan, but it also leaves the central questions unresolved: whether nurses accept the proposal, whether negotiators return to the table, and whether a new strike date becomes necessary.

For now, patients should treat the Oct. 14 strike as postponed rather than canceled. Mass General Brigham’s public materials say the hospital will provide further updates as the vote process develops. The next decisive event is the nurses’ ratification vote; until that result is known, neither a new contract nor a future walkout can be reported as certain.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Brigham Nurses Postpone Strike for Contract Vote
seoDescription: More than 4,000 Brigham nurses postponed their planned Oct. 14 strike to vote on Mass General Brigham’s latest contract proposal.
